name: QtAV
baseline: VLC media player (CPU usage on Android, 10-bit H.264 playback)
metric: other (CPU usage during playback; claimed lower)
workload: Playback of a 10-bit H.264 video on an HTC Butterfly S phone, CPU usage compared with VLC.
claimed_speedup: About 10% less CPU usage than VLC for a 10-bit H.264 video on an HTC Butterfly S (snippet of a forum post, not opened). The repo wiki page 'The Most Efficient VDA Decoder on OSX' also says 'The performance is the best now. Better than any other players.' with no numbers.
hardware: HTC Butterfly S (Android phone), per search snippet; CPU model not stated
stars_or_usage: 4.3k stars; listed on the FFmpeg projects page per its README
tradeoffs: Qt plus FFmpeg playback framework with hardware decoders (DXVA2, VAAPI, VideoToolbox, CedarX, CUDA) and OpenGL/ES2 rendering for Hi10P and other formats. The library is LGPL v2.1, the player example is GPL v3, and FFmpeg licensing applies on top. The author says he no longer develops QtAV and points to his newer mdk-sdk.
caveats: Weak evidence, tier C at most. The only number is one anecdote from the QtAV announcement thread on the Qt forum ('A video player based on Qt and FFmpeg', post id 21312, circa the QtAV 1.3.x era in 2014); forum.qt.io is unreachable from this environment so the page was NOT opened and the figure comes from WebSearch snippets only (snippet only). The poster appears to be the project author. No VLC version, build, video file, or CPU model is given and the figure is a single device test with no methodology. A search snippet also showed a user reporting that VLC plays full-HD video more smoothly than QtAV, so the claim is contested. The repo README and wiki otherwise contain only qualitative claims (best performance, better than any other players, low memory vs mplayer) with no numbers. A Qt-forum claim of lower memory than mplayer is likewise unmeasured. The README says the author stopped developing QtAV.

name: SAIL
baseline: stb_image, FreeImage and OpenImageIO (JPEG decode time); Boost.GIL, CImg, DevIL and SDL_Image also measured
metric: other (wall-clock time to decode an image and output default pixels, microseconds)
workload: Load JPEG (grayscale and YCbCr) and PNG (grayscale and RGBA) files at 100x67, 1000x669, 6000x4016 and 15000x10040 (PNG heights 71, 709, 4256, 10640) through each library's default path with no explicit pixel conversion; wall-clock microseconds.
claimed_speedup: Chart labels in the project's BENCHMARKS charts (microseconds, lower is better). JPEG YCbCr 1000x669: SAIL 4577 vs stb_image 7842, OpenImageIO 5470, FreeImage 5029, DevIL 4597, SDL_Image 4740, WIC 4726 (1.71x faster than stb_image, derived from page data). JPEG YCbCr 6000x4016: SAIL 226067 vs stb_image 351115, OpenImageIO 262450, FreeImage 237112, DevIL 226361, SDL_Image 229923, but WIC 209636 is faster (1.55x vs stb_image, derived from page data). JPEG Gray 6000x4016: SAIL 72449 vs stb_image 103020, OpenImageIO 83176, FreeImage 72756, DevIL 72261, WIC 70683 (1.42x vs stb_image, derived from page data). PNG RGBA 6000x4256: SAIL 515651 vs OpenImageIO 647908, FreeImage 532293, but stb_image 334286 and WIC 348043 are faster. PNG Gray 6000x4256: SAIL 142685 vs OpenImageIO 155180, FreeImage 144725, but stb_image 97276 and WIC 103314 are faster.
compiler_and_flags: MSVC 2019 x64 on Windows 7 x64; the sail-benchmark harness (Google Benchmark) is built in the CMake Release configuration with libraries installed through vcpkg; no further flags or library versions are stated
hardware: Lenovo ThinkPad W540, Intel Core i7-4800MQ, power cable connected, Maximum Performance power plan
stars_or_usage: 359 stars; also on Conan, vcpkg, brew and PyPI (sailpy)
tradeoffs: C11 library with C++11 and Python bindings that wraps libjpeg-turbo, libpng, giflib, libtiff, libwebp, libheif, libjxl, openjpeg and others behind one API with pluggable codecs, so it adds an indirection layer rather than new codecs. Four API levels (junior to deep diver). Decoding focus; metadata handling and format coverage depend on the bundled codec wrappers.
caveats: First-party benchmark by the SAIL author (harness in his HappySeaFox/sail-benchmark repo, MIT, compiled from public code), tier C because compiler flags beyond the Release build type, library versions and iteration counts are not stated and there is no variance. The per-size numbers exist only as labels inside chart images (.github/benchmarks/*.png, embedded in BENCHMARKS.md), not as text; they were read from the images. SAIL is a wrapper over libjpeg-turbo and libpng, so on JPEG it ties the other libjpeg-turbo based loaders (DevIL, FreeImage and SDL_Image are within about 0-5% of it, which is within noise) and the headline win is mainly over stb_image and the non-turbo or higher-overhead paths (OpenImageIO, CImg, Boost.GIL). On PNG SAIL is slower: stb_image and Windows WIC decode 6000x4256 PNG about 1.5x faster (RGBA 334286 and 348043 vs 515651 microseconds; Gray 97276 and 103314 vs 142685), and WIC also beats SAIL on large JPEGs. The test machine is a Windows 7 laptop (Haswell, circa 2014) and the README charts may predate the harness, which was last updated 2026-01-22 and now also lists gdk-pixbuf, GraphicsMagick and OpenCV that do not appear in the README charts. The libjpeg-turbo baseline itself was not measured directly. The lead listed the repo as happy-sea-fox/sail; the opened repository is HappySeaFox/sail.
